newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Sept 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Sept 26.

text.p: Japanese trading company Marubeni Corp and Hitachi Ltd plan to start a type of cable television (CATV) service in Yokohama from July 1997 by using optical-fibre communications through Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp.

Eight of fourteen car parts makers are expected to see their current earnings fall in the year ending March 1997. Six out of the eight makers, including NOK Corp and Zexel Corp, are expected to see their current earnings fall due to weak vehicle production in Japan. In contrast, six car parts makers, including Nippondenso Co Ltd, are expected to see their current profits rise, helped by strong sales of cellular phones and non-car parts.

Japan's biggest convenience store operator, Seven-Eleven Japan Co Ltd, increased its sales by about six percent to 790 billion yen from a year earlier in the first half ended August 31, 1996, outselling its parent company Ito-Yokado Co Ltd by about eight billion yen and becoming the second biggest retailer after Daiei Inc.

TKI Semiconductor Ltd, a joint venture launched by Texas Instruments Inc and Kobe Steel Ltd, plans to invest four billion yen to boost production of dynamic random access memory chips (DRAMs) by renovating its old facilities in Hyogo Prefecture by year-end in an effort to cut costs.

Orix Corp plans to start a leasing venture in Egypt next January, in cooperation with an Egyptian state-run bank and other companies. The new company, capitalised at 590 million yen, is the first venture set up by Orix in the Middle East/Africa region. It will be 23 percent owned each by Orix and Orix Leading Pakistan Ltd, 39 percent by the central bank of Egypt and its affiliates and 15 percent by a World Bank-affiliated financial corporation.

Sumitomo Metal Industries Ltd plans to set up a joint venture in Thailand to process high-quality wire rods for car parts, aiming to start production from October 1997. The new company, capitalised at 540 million yen, will be owned 50 percent by Sumitomo Metal, 30 percent by Sumitomo Corp and 10 percent each by a Sumitomo Metal group wire-rod processor and a Siam Steel Pipe group company in Thailand.

Sapporo Breweries Ltd and Marubeni Corp plan to launch a joint venture to produce and sell Sapporo-brand beers in China from the end of 1997, in cooperation with two beer makers in China. The joint venture will be capitalised at $20 million.

Fujitsu General Ltd plans to sell a wide-screen television set with a 42-inch plasma display panel (PDP) in December for 1.2 million yen. Fujitsu General will sell the PDP television earlier than NEC Corp and Philips Electronics NV, which have already announced plans to sell PDP televisions.
